issues.description: Pre-filter regexes lack a stated soundness invariant
issues.detail: Every pre-filter here rests on the same correctness claim: the regex matches a superset of values the rule would ever report on, so an early return is provably safe. That invariant is not written down anywhere. Future maintainers adding new keywords (e.g. new font-weight names, new keyframe selectors, new media operators) will silently break the optimization by leaving the regex out of sync with the rule logic. A one-line literate comment above each HAS_* regex stating 'NECESSARY condition: if this fails, the rule cannot report' would make the contract explicit and auditable.

The PR title is 'Fix *-notation performance' but no benchmark numbers, profile, or corpus is cited in the description. Knuth's rule applies: optimize the 3% that matters, and only after measuring. The changes are plausibly in a hot path (rules called on every declaration/at-rule across large stylesheets) and the early-return pattern is sound, but the PR should attach before/after timings on a representative corpus so reviewers can confirm this is the 3% and not the 97%.

issues.description: selectorRegex = /./ is a less readable 'match anything' sentinel
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, the 'percentage-unless-within-keyword-only-block' branch sets selectorRegex = /./ purely to make walkRules visit every rule. Cleaner to dispatch: call walkRules(selectorRegex, cb) when a filter exists, walkRules(cb) when it does not. The /./ trick also has a minor semantic edge: it would skip a rule with an empty selector string, where the unfiltered form would not. Invalid CSS in practice, but the dispatch form removes the question.

issues.description: Behavior change: :not / pseudo-element matching becomes case-insensitive
issues.detail: selector-not-notation previously did selector.includes(':not(') (case-sensitive) and now uses /:not\(/i. CSS pseudo-classes are case-insensitive per spec, so the new behavior is arguably more correct, but it is a behavior change that should be called out in the changeset. Worth a sentence so downstream users with :NOT( in fixtures know what changed.

issues.description: Asymmetric case-insensitivity flag between HAS_NAMED and HAS_NUMERIC
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED has the /i flag, HAS_NUMERIC does not. In practice harmless because numeric font-weights are pure digits, but the asymmetry invites a future maintainer to add an alphabetic numeric synonym (e.g. a hypothetical 'normal-as-400') without thinking about case. A short comment '// digits only; no case flag needed' would close the loop.

issues.description: Pre-filters do not exclude string/comment contexts; acceptable but worth noting
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED on a font shorthand value like 'font: 16px "bold serif"' will trigger the slow path because 'bold' appears inside a font-family string. Same for /url\(/i triggering on @import layer names that contain the substring url, and /:/ triggering on attribute selectors like a[href*=":"]. None of these are correctness bugs (slow path still produces correct output), but they do bound the achievable speedup. Worth one comment per file noting the filter is a coarse necessary condition, not a precise one.

review.summary: The optimization pattern is algorithmically sound: each pre-filter regex is a necessary condition for the rule to ever report, so an early-return is safe and the asymptotic work stays the same while the constant factor on the common (no-op) path drops substantially. Data structure choices are appropriate — module-level RegExp construction, not per-call. The directional logic is correct on the cases I worked through (font-weight numeric vs named, import url vs string, keyframe keyword vs percentage including mixed selectors, media prefix vs context including <= and >=). Main gaps are Knuth-flavored rather than correctness-flavored: the soundness invariant ('regex matches a superset of reportable values') is not written down, no measurements are cited to justify the 'performance' framing, and there are a couple of small readability and consistency nits (selectorRegex = /./, asymmetric /i flags, an undocumented case-sensitivity change in selector-not-notation). UNDER-AUDITED bordering on RIGOROUS — promote to RIGOROUS by adding the invariant comments and a benchmark line in the changeset.
